Comprehensive Accountability
Maximizing the progress of all students toward career and college
readiness requires attention toward multiple points of influence.

Institutional – Schools, Districts
Personnel – Principals and Teacher
Programs – Curriculum and educational programs
Students

State and Federal mandates have often been piecemeal (schools or
teachers/principals). Groups feel like scapegoats.

Everyone plays a role from policy makers to parents.

Accountability and Student Growth

Coherent Accountability

Accountability initiative spread across different levels are often
incoherent

Indicators at the state, district, school, and teacher level often do
not “speak” to each other.

Goal: Create a unified indicator system that speaks to all
stakeholder goals: Comprehensive and coherent so that
participants are tied to “translatable” goals.

Accountability and Student Growth

Status Quo
The Center for Assessment is currently working with approximately 20 states on
growth and accountability.

A variety of use cases:

RttT states: Focus is on teacher evaluation

Non RttT states: Diagnostic uses of growth data, institutional evaluation
(including growth for AYP purposes), program evaluation.

Some use cases are more personal than others.

Recommendation: Be deliberate but don’t rush. Less personal use cases allow
stakeholders to become familiar with the indicators.
